answer: Each identity backs one copper ripple coil, velvet-wrapped, with a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it files ripple reading, serial, and load, key-signed. An auditor recomputes the ripple from the coil-turn table and checks serial and velvet wrap. Over 3 percent off, a reused serial, or one coil for two identities burns the bond. First costs 36; kth 36+5(k-1); 1000th 5031; 1000 fakes 2,533,500 plus 70,000 bonded, each coil needing winding, wrap, and load. A rented-coil ring fails: one serial cannot yield two curves matching the table. Honest identities pay 36 once, bond returned after audit.
